To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aminobisphosphonates (ABP), such as zoledronate, activate T cells in systemic sclerosis (SSC) and healthy donor patients to produce procoagulant tissue factor (TF) on monocytes.
aminobisphosphonates induce secretion of TNF-α by Vγδ2+ T lymphocytes, which may lead to TNFR-1-dependent induction of pro-coagulant TF-2+ monocytes in certain clinical settings, such as SSc.
aminobisphosphonates (ABP), such as zoledronate, can activate γδ T cells in vivo and in vitro, and induce an inflammatory response in a subset of patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Vγ9δ1 T cells in systemic sclerosis (SSC), an autoimmune disease characterized by fibrosis and microvascular damage.
the possible role of bisphosphonate-induced γδ T cells in the pathogenesis of thrombosis in patients with systemic sclerosis.
the role of Vγ9δ1+ T lymphocytes in the pathogenesis of SSc and their potential contribution to the development of thrombosis in SSc patients.

the combination of the two proinflammatory stimuli, i.e., Zol and LPS, induced TF-1+ on CD14+ MCs in both SSc and HD PBMC, but only the Zol-induced TF+ was blocked by an anti-TNFα monoclonal antibody in PBMC of SSc patients.
Zol-induced activation of γδT cells in vivo can induce a prothrombogenic state in monocytes in vitro, which may contribute to thrombotic events in certain patients, e.g., in SSc.
Zol-induced TNFα production by γδ T cells may lead, via an as yet unidentified mechanism, to monocyte procoagulant activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Vγ9δ T cells of SSc patients may acquire an abnormal phenotype that renders them more susceptible to activation by ABP.

aminobisphosphonates, such as zoledronate, can induce a prothrombosis pathway in patients with systemic sclerosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Zol, a commonly used drug, induces a procoagulant phenotype in PBMCs, and that the procoagulant response is enhanced in SSc patients, possibly leading to clinically relevant thromboses.
aminobisphosphonates may induce thrombosis by inducing the expression of tissue factor on monocytes in a TNF-α dependent manner.
aminobisphophonates can induce an inflammatory response that may lead to thrombosis.
